belongs_to: Printed answer to Figure it Out Q2 (i): 'Draw a quadrilateral whose diagonals have equal lengths of 8 cm that bisect each other and intersect at 30 degrees' - the construction drawn for (i)
description: A long horizontal segment AB (A at the left end, B at the right end), midpoint O marked with a filled dot (letter O above it). Small tick marks on AB: one at about the middle of AO and one at about the middle of OB; the label '4 cm' is printed under the left tick (below AO) and '8 cm' under O (below the line, right of O). A long straight line l through O rising to the right at 30 degrees to OB, with arrowheads at both ends (the upper-right arrowhead is labelled 'l'). The 30 degrees angle is marked with an arc between OB and OC and labelled '30 degrees'. C lies on l above-right of O (OC labelled '4 cm' along the line, rotated) with a short compass arc crossing l at C; D lies on l below-left of O with a short compass arc crossing l at D (OD = OC = 4 cm). The quadrilateral ADBC is drawn with its four sides AC (long, upper), CB (short, right), BD (long, lower), DA (short, left); the diagonals AB and CD are drawn. Letters A, B, C, D, O, l.
unclear: Positions of the two small ticks on AB are approximate (one in the middle of AO and one in the middle of OB).

belongs_to: Printed answers, Figure it Out Q3: 'Consider a circle with centre O. PL and AM are two perpendicular diameters. What is the figure APML?'
description: A circle with centre O (small dot, letter O just above-right of it). Two perpendicular diameters: horizontal PL (P at the left end, L at the right end) and vertical AM (A at the top end, M at the bottom end). The four endpoints A, P, M, L lie on the circle and the quadrilateral APML (sides AP, PM, ML, LA) is drawn inside, so it looks like a diamond/square with the two diameters as its diagonals. Letters A, P, O, L, M. No tick marks or right-angle marks.
unclear: The figure sits between the question and the word 'Ans.'; it already draws the quadrilateral APML, so it can be read as the question figure or as the answer picture.

belongs_to: Printed answer to Figure it Out Q4: 'two sticks of equal length and a thread - how do we make an exact 90 degrees?' (sticks AB and CD, thread ACB)
description: Two equal sticks crossing at their midpoints at O: stick AB horizontal (A at the left end, B at the right end, both ends dotted) and stick CD slanted (C up-left, D down-right of O, steeply sloped, about 60 degrees below horizontal on the right). ONE tick on each of the four half-sticks AO, OB, CO, OD (equal halves). The thread is drawn as two dotted straight segments from A up to C and from C to B, making the triangle ACB. Filled dots at A, O, B. Letters C (top), A, O, B, D (bottom right). No angle values printed on the figure.
